head: working-tree
subject: MQTT filter validation reports wildcard presence in one scan
change: validateTopicFilter and hasWildcards previously scanned a Topic Filter twice: validTopicFilterLevels validated wildcard placement, then retained lookups called hasWildcards on the effective filter. validTopicFilterLevelsKind now returns null for invalid, false for a valid literal filter, and true for a valid wildcard filter; validSharedTopicFilterKind returns the same kind for the nested filter of a shared subscription. validateTopicFilterKind exposes the combined result, validateTopicFilter routes through it, and the retained matchInto/deliveriesInto paths branch on the returned flag instead of calling hasWildcards. The accepted grammar, '$share/' validation, and error precedence are unchanged.

mqtt_interop.note: full Mosquitto-derived broker configuration matrix, including retained state, shared subscriptions, ACL reloads and persistence.

notes: The exact scenario is the direct beneficiary: one wildcard scan instead of two per lookup, measured at 20.0 -> 17.0 ns/op in an exact-only batch (8/8 wins) and 20.5 -> 17.0 in the full batch (1.206x). The selective devices/+/state scenario shows a consistent 1.8% delta in two focused batches. That delta is attributed to code layout, not validation cost: validation runs once per lookup while the scenario performs 4,096 matches, so removing one scan cannot account for a 2 us difference; a noinline variant measured the same 0.982x. The change is retained as an explicit trade-off because the exact win is 17.6-20.6% and the selective replay remains within its historical cross-batch range (105.7-113.1 us). Wildcard, hash, and subtree scenarios are otherwise neutral. The host was loaded during the batches (load average roughly 5 to 20), so only interleaved ratios are claimed.
